title: Apple launches research study to explore the use of AI for health

quotes.text: The Apple Health AI Usage Study is open to up to 200,000 eligible participants age 21 and older across the United States.
quotes.for: Participant cap, age requirement, and U.S. availability.

quotes.text: The study is designed from the ground up with privacy protections, transparency, and clinical guardrails, and study data will not be used to train AI models.
quotes.for: Privacy protections, guardrails, and no-training pledge.

quotes.text: The study app is not meant to diagnose or treat any condition, or replace the advice of medical professionals.
quotes.for: Non-diagnostic disclaimer for the study app.

quotes.text: At Apple, we believe responsible innovation starts with scientific rigor and clinical grounding.
quotes.for: Statement from Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple's vice president of Health and Fitness.

quotes.text: Patients and clinicians are both turning to AI, but the tools they use are being built and tested in separate worlds
quotes.for: Statement from Robert M. Wachter, M.D., chair of UCSF's Department of Medicine.

quotes.text: Consumer health technologies powered by LLMs may at times offer responses that are incomplete or unclear
quotes.for: Apple's stated rationale for the study.

quotes.text: To join, participants must have an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone (iPhone 15 Pro or later) running iOS 26 or later.
quotes.for: Apple's device requirement.

quotes.text: Apple has implemented security measures to protect the study data it maintains
quotes.for: Apple's only description of its security measures.

quotes.text: Apple today announced the launch of the Apple Health AI Usage Study in the United States, a virtual research study and associated app designed to advance the understanding of how people interact with conversational health AI tools.
quotes.for: Launch and scope.

quotes.text: By examining what drives user trust, the quality of responses, comprehension, and everyday health actions, the study aims to inform the responsible design of health AI experiences for Apple and the industry.
quotes.for: Research aims.

quotes.text: The study brings together medically grounded AI technology developed by OpenEvidence with an Apple-designed research experience.
quotes.for: Collaboration.

quotes.text: Participants will be able to ask the study app everyday health questions; explore complex medical information communicated with approachable language; and see linked, peer-reviewed clinical citations that ground each response.
quotes.for: App answers and citations.

quotes.text: Participants can also choose to share HealthKit data types — such as resting heart rate, activity, sleep, or lab results — to explore how personal data integration impacts relevance and understanding.
quotes.for: Optional health metrics.

quotes.text: The study app features safety guardrails that are intended to detect certain concerning questions and suggest that a participant follow up with a provider or other resources if needed.
quotes.for: Guardrails.

quotes.text: medical information from established sources such as The New England Journal of Medicine, Journal of the American Medical Association, and Nature
quotes.for: Named clinical publications.

quotes.text: Participants retain control over whether to share any HealthKit metrics or survey responses
quotes.for: Participant control.

quotes.text: The study will also explore how health AI can potentially help participants better prepare for clinical visits with their own doctors.
quotes.for: Visit preparation research.

title: Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health

quotes.text: The company is aiming to run this study with up to 200,000 participants for more than 12 months.
quotes.for: Planned study duration of more than 12 months.

quotes.text: The company said that OpenEvidence deletes the query and response data after 24 hours.
quotes.for: OpenEvidence's 24-hour deletion window for query and response data.

quotes.text: earlier this year, OpenAI said users were asking over 300 million health-related queries
quotes.for: OpenAI's reported volume of weekly health-related queries.

quotes.text: using iPhone 15 or later, and running iOS 26 or later, with Apple Intelligence enabled
quotes.for: TechCrunch's wording of the device requirement.

quotes.text: and it will guide users to specific providers for answers related to concerning medical issues
quotes.for: Referral of concerning questions to providers.

quotes.text: Users can rate those answers and provide feedback about the responses; they’ll also be asked to participate in monthly surveys.
quotes.for: Ratings and monthly surveys.

title: Apple Opens U.S. Study of Trust in Conversational Health AI

quotes.text: The App Store listing says the app can be used to understand symptoms or conditions, put personal health data in context, prepare for a medical visit, and build a personalized exercise or meal plan.
quotes.for: Use cases described in the App Store listing.

quotes.text: The App Store privacy label says user identifiers may be collected and linked to identity for analytics and app functionality, while diagnostics and performance data may be collected without being linked to identity.
quotes.for: App Store privacy label disclosures on linked identifiers.
